arcs.title: The River Before the Fields
arcs.situation: The first farming households reach a European river world already anchored by settlement, burial and exchange.
arcs.mechanism: People carry seed, livestock, tools and learned routines together across the Aegean and into the Danube corridor.
arcs.turn: The field arrives as a complete living system rather than an isolated crop.
arcs.consequence: Europe's inhabited river frontier becomes the meeting place of two durable ways of life.
arcs.handoff: Arrival creates the harder problem: a harvest must now carry a household through the year.

arcs.title: The Harvest Had to Last
arcs.situation: A farming household faces winter, spoilage and the obligation to reserve seed for spring.
arcs.mechanism: Food, reserve and seed compete inside one finite store while river and farming communities exchange people and practices.
arcs.turn: Grain eaten now cannot answer scarcity or return to the soil.
arcs.consequence: Farming becomes a discipline of deferred use and inherited obligation.
arcs.handoff: Once stores and households endure, the settlement itself can outlive its builders.

arcs.title: The House Outlives Its Builders
arcs.situation: Timber houses decay while repeated rebuilding fixes communities to the same European ground.
arcs.mechanism: Household growth, field clearance, herd traffic and settlement memory expand across the loess plains.
arcs.turn: A family economy becomes a demographic force able to remake whole landscapes.
arcs.consequence: Europe becomes a continent of fields, herds and long-lived settlements.
arcs.handoff: That settled order now faces a mobile power arriving from the steppe.

arcs.title: A World That Could Move
arcs.situation: Beyond Europe's last fields, wealth lives in herds and can move away from scarcity or danger.
arcs.mechanism: Ox-drawn wagons join animals, people and possessions into mobile households with a wider practical reach.
arcs.turn: The household itself becomes transportable.
arcs.consequence: Mobility gives armed, patrilineal groups a new field of power west of the Black Sea.
arcs.handoff: Moving households begin to claim land through fathers, graves and force.

arcs.title: The Fathers Disappear
arcs.situation: Steppe groups enter settled Europe carrying paternal authority, mobile wealth and an inherited sacred language.
arcs.mechanism: Conquest, demographic asymmetry, household formation and descent reorder paternal lines and speech.
arcs.turn: Across several regions, many sampled local male lines disappear as incoming lines spread.
arcs.consequence: Steppe ancestry, Indo-European languages and religious grammar become European inheritances.
arcs.handoff: Bronze gives the inherited order new weapons, symbols, routes and heroic forms.

arcs.title: Bronze Crosses the Sea
arcs.situation: Europe enters an age whose decisive metal depends on materials found far apart.
arcs.mechanism: Mines, passes, ships, palaces and writing join copper, tin, grain, cloth and authority.
arcs.turn: The sea becomes a road across which rulers can count and command a connected world.
arcs.consequence: European power acquires a metal, a maritime scale and palace institutions.
arcs.handoff: Beyond the palaces, northern Europe makes the bronze world its own.

arcs.title: The Heroic Age
arcs.situation: Nordic farms, Aegean warriors and an international ship carry different forms of one bronze civilisation.
arcs.mechanism: Craft, rank, sacred image, cargo and trained violence make power visible and portable.
arcs.turn: The palace network burns and its archives fall silent.
arcs.consequence: Sung heroic memory preserves names, weapons and ideals after the scribal order disappears.
arcs.handoff: The singer carries the age into the public world of the Greek polis.

arcs.title: The City Steps into the Light
arcs.situation: Greek communities inherit no restored palace capable of governing them.
arcs.mechanism: Inscribed law, public office, sanctuary, agora and colonial foundation make authority visible and repeatable.
arcs.turn: Citizenship becomes a bounded public status rather than attendance upon a king's hall.
arcs.consequence: The polis establishes the first recognisably European public world.
arcs.handoff: Sparta and Athens now construct citizen bodies strong enough to command war.

arcs.title: Greece Defends Its Freedom
arcs.situation: Independent cities face Persian imperial power with no single Greek state above them.
arcs.mechanism: Athenian civic geography and participation combine with Spartan leadership and allied land and sea strength.
arcs.turn: The coalition survives because different poleis supply capacities none possesses alone.
arcs.consequence: Greek autonomy endures and citizenship acquires unmatched political reach in Athens.
arcs.handoff: Victory turns alliance into command and opens a struggle between rival meanings of freedom.

arcs.title: The War for the Greek World
arcs.situation: Athenian protection and Spartan autonomy have become incompatible claims over the Greek world.
arcs.mechanism: Fortification, fleet, allied resources, Persian finance and constitutional adaptation prolong the war.
arcs.turn: Sparta wins only after changing its system and mastering the sea.
arcs.consequence: Hegemony fails to end the civic argument; councils, assemblies and public law continue under later powers.
arcs.handoff: Rome enters a Mediterranean already filled with citizens and scales their political form.

arcs.title: Power Without a King
arcs.situation: Rome removes its king but cannot dispense with effective public command.
arcs.mechanism: Divided offices, public procedures, citizen conflict and graded settlements make power answerable and recoverable.
arcs.turn: Defeat teaches Rome to restore armies and political relationships instead of accepting final collapse.
arcs.consequence: A republic with multiple forms of incorporation begins to dominate Italy.
arcs.handoff: Roads and colonies turn those relationships into an army that can return again and again.

arcs.title: The Italian Engine
arcs.situation: Rome must assemble and replace forces across a peninsula of unequal allies and citizens.
arcs.mechanism: Roads, colonies, treaties, allied manpower and differentiated obligations convert territory into sustained war capacity.
arcs.turn: Hannibal wins great battles but cannot dissolve enough of the alliance system to end the war.
arcs.consequence: Mediterranean conquest enlarges Rome while Italian allies force citizenship into the centre of the constitutional order.
arcs.handoff: Long commands and conquered wealth now return to institutions built for annual civic competition.

arcs.title: The Roman Name
arcs.situation: Personal armies have broken the Republic while the provinces still require durable government.
arcs.mechanism: Imperial command rests on professional armies, census, cities, service, local office and widening citizenship.
arcs.turn: The Roman political identity becomes provincial before Caracalla makes citizenship the normal free status.
arcs.consequence: Much of Europe lives inside a common Roman civic and legal order.
arcs.handoff: Christian emperors and bishops inherit a public already joined by law, city and Roman name.

arcs.title: The Sign and New Rome
arcs.situation: A persecuted Church meets an emperor seeking victory, unity and a more strategic imperial centre.
arcs.mechanism: Legal protection, patronage and urban foundation bring Christian worship into public Roman space.
arcs.turn: Constantine founds New Rome where the Bosporus joins continents and seas.
arcs.consequence: Christianity gains imperial scale while Constantinople acquires the position from which Rome can continue.
arcs.handoff: The emperor now summons bishops and makes doctrine an affair of the Roman world.

arcs.title: Faith Becomes Imperial Business
arcs.situation: Christian bishops possess competing formulations while the empire needs a common public confession.
arcs.mechanism: Council, creed, imperial action, walls and urban institutions bind Church and state without erasing their distinct authority.
arcs.turn: The creed survives emperors who try to direct it, while bishops acquire durable civic weight.
arcs.consequence: Constantinople becomes a fortified Christian capital and Nicene faith an authorised imperial order.
arcs.handoff: Doctrine, city and office now require lasting forms in law, stone and worship.

arcs.title: Stone, Law and Dome
arcs.situation: The western throne disappears while the eastern Roman state retains capital, law and imperial office.
arcs.mechanism: Council, codification, architecture and organised restoration make Christian Rome materially visible.
arcs.turn: Hagia Sophia rises after revolt as Justinian's recovered provinces strain the resources of the centre.
arcs.consequence: Roman law and Christian kingship survive in a renewed eastern empire facing costly frontiers.
arcs.handoff: In the west, bishops, monasteries and kings rebuild the inheritance without one emperor.

arcs.title: Rule Outlives Rome
arcs.situation: Western imperial command recedes while cities, property, literacy and Christian institutions remain.
arcs.mechanism: Bishops, baptism and monastic rule convert inherited resources into government, legitimacy and durable time.
arcs.turn: A rule copied across borders proves that an institution can survive the ruler and realm around it.
arcs.consequence: Roman Christian civilisation acquires local bodies capable of carrying it through political fragmentation.
arcs.handoff: Kingship now joins sacred rite, conquest and the written instruments of wider government.

arcs.title: The Written Commonwealth
arcs.situation: Frankish rulers need legitimacy and reach beyond the movement of their own court.
arcs.mechanism: Anointing, conquest, capitulary, corrected book, delegated judgment and imperial title carry authority across distance.
arcs.turn: The heirs divide the realm, but the written and Christian commonwealth survives the dynasty's partition.
arcs.consequence: Europe can retain shared institutions while political centres multiply.
arcs.handoff: Northern violence and eastern missions test how far the commonwealth can expand.

arcs.title: Europe Meets at Gniezno
arcs.situation: Scandinavian ships, eastern rulers and rival mission roads enlarge Europe's political and Christian field.
arcs.mechanism: Trade, conquest, baptism, language, alphabet, shrine, gift and archbishopric create recognised centres.
arcs.turn: At Gniezno an emperor recognises a Polish Christian order without absorbing it.
arcs.consequence: Europe can meet as one civilisation through several rulers and churches.
arcs.handoff: That plurality sharpens the conflict over who appoints bishops and possesses ecclesiastical office.

arcs.title: A Papacy Learns to Govern
arcs.situation: Imperial intervention rescues the Roman see while revealing how dependent its reform remains.
arcs.mechanism: Personnel, synods, legates, privileges and ordered election turn reform into repeatable government.
arcs.turn: Milan's urban struggle makes clerical office a public jurisdictional question.
arcs.consequence: The papacy acquires instruments able to project judgment beyond Rome.
arcs.handoff: The bishop's combined altar, estate and royal service brings the two governments into direct collision.

arcs.title: Ring and Crown
arcs.situation: Bishops hold sacramental office and temporal power that neither pope nor king can abandon.
arcs.mechanism: Appointment, prohibition, excommunication, oath, princely reception and penance make authority depend on recognised acts.
arcs.turn: Canossa restores communion without deciding the German crown or the boundary of power.
arcs.consequence: The conflict survives its most famous reconciliation and becomes a struggle between organised jurisdictions.
arcs.handoff: War, imprisonment and failed settlements now force the acts of investiture apart.

arcs.title: Two Jurisdictions
arcs.situation: Possession of Rome and coercive privilege fail to create a settlement either government can sustain.
arcs.mechanism: Regional compromise, reciprocal instruments and distinct ceremonies divide spiritual investiture from temporal regalia.
arcs.turn: Worms makes each side recognise acts that belong to the other.
arcs.consequence: Latin Europe contains two public jurisdictions that cannot fully absorb one another.
arcs.handoff: Other European bodies can now seek office, property and jurisdiction in their own name.

arcs.title: Marriage Leaves the Clan
arcs.situation: Lineages keep marriage, inheritance and obligation inside dense kin networks.
arcs.mechanism: The Church widens prohibited kin, makes consent decisive and receives land into enduring religious houses.
arcs.turn: Two speaking persons become the legal makers of marriage.
arcs.consequence: Households must seek bonds beyond the clan and property can leave the lineage circuit.
arcs.handoff: A monastery demonstrates how unrelated people can become one durable house.

arcs.title: Bodies Made by Choice
arcs.situation: Europeans need reliable cooperation among people not born into one lineage.
arcs.mechanism: Vow, rule, common property, mutual aid, oath, election and seal construct monasteries, guilds and communes.
arcs.turn: A sworn crowd acquires officers and acts as one government.
arcs.consequence: Chosen association becomes a practical source of authority, care and civic order.
arcs.handoff: The common body must now keep property and identity while its members change.

arcs.title: The Institution Outlives Us
arcs.situation: Shared property and distant members expose associations to mistrust and mortality.
arcs.mechanism: Divided custody, legal personality, privilege, record and succession separate the body from any one member.
arcs.turn: Students abroad use corporate organisation to become powerful strangers.
arcs.consequence: Europe learns to build institutions whose offices, possessions and purposes endure across generations.
arcs.handoff: These bodies send promises, ventures and capital farther than their founders can travel.

arcs.title: The Written Voyage
arcs.situation: Mediterranean merchants act across rulers, currencies and seas no single government controls.
arcs.mechanism: Notary, fair calendar, commenda and bounded exposure give the voyage a durable legal form.
arcs.turn: The contract possesses a route and a limit of loss before the ship possesses a favourable wind.
arcs.consequence: Strangers can join capital and skill in repeatable enterprise without placing every possession at risk.
arcs.handoff: The venture now requires courts, account money and settlement across the continent.

arcs.title: The Promise Travels
arcs.situation: Long-distance exchange remains vulnerable to unsafe roads, changing coin and maritime danger.
arcs.mechanism: Safe conduct, money of account, netting, ledger and insurance make obligation and risk portable.
arcs.turn: Metal settles only the remainder after written claims have crossed the Alps.
arcs.consequence: European commerce gains memory, priced risk and routes capable of joining north and south.
arcs.handoff: At Bruges, the ledger road meets the shipping world of Lübeck and Bergen.

arcs.title: The Northern Year
arcs.situation: Norway's seasonal catch and Baltic grain must cross long, cold routes to reach the people who need them.
arcs.mechanism: Drying, navigation, reciprocal cargo, privilege, yard government and discipline make Bergen a northern commercial hinge.
arcs.turn: The Bryggen yard becomes a corporate machine able to preserve foreign rights in daily work.
arcs.consequence: Distance becomes a durable exchange between coast, city and crown.
arcs.handoff: The same discipline must now join separate city governments into common action.

arcs.title: Cities Act Together
arcs.situation: No Hanseatic sovereign can command the towns, their rulers or the exposed ends of trade.
arcs.mechanism: Delegated consent, diet, embargo, contributed fleet and four Kontore turn agreement into selective force and intelligence.
arcs.turn: Separate seals authorise one covenant without surrendering the governments behind them.
arcs.consequence: Northern cities can bargain with kings and defend a continental field of trade together.
arcs.handoff: The Empire gives this European habit of agreement a larger constitutional home.

arcs.title: The Travelling Crown
arcs.situation: A Roman imperial crown governs central Europe without a permanent capital or uniform administrative state.
arcs.mechanism: Itinerary, charter, custom, urban law, princely right and electoral procedure carry authority across a plural realm.
arcs.turn: The Golden Bull makes succession dependable without making the crown hereditary.
arcs.consequence: The Empire turns accumulated rights and election into a durable constitution.
arcs.handoff: Estates now need permanent procedures for law, peace and common action.

arcs.title: Liberty Inside Order
arcs.situation: Feud, religious division and territorial variety threaten the public peace.
arcs.mechanism: Diet, court, circles and confessional settlement give unequal powers shared instruments of government.
arcs.turn: Westphalia preserves the mosaic by making negotiation and jurisdiction continuous.
arcs.consequence: Real liberties endure because they live inside a common imperial order.
arcs.handoff: Those distributed powers now assemble to defend Christian Europe at its frontiers.

arcs.title: The Broken Frontiers
arcs.situation: Christian polities lose Iberia and Anatolia to external conquest while western and eastern institutions remain divided.
arcs.mechanism: Northern refuge, chartered settlement, coalition battle and armed pilgrimage rebuild positions after catastrophe.
arcs.turn: The Fourth Crusade breaks Constantinople's defence from inside Christendom.
arcs.consequence: European survival depends on repeatedly rebuilding lines that victories and internal fracture can both destroy.
arcs.handoff: The eastern Roman capital falls, and the defence moves to Belgrade, the Danube and the Mediterranean.

arcs.title: The Frontier Turns
arcs.situation: Ottoman conquest presses through Constantinople and the Danube toward central Europe.
arcs.mechanism: Fortified cities, military-frontier communities, island harbours, coalition fleets and relief armies hold successive gates.
arcs.turn: Vienna's defence in 1683 buys time for European roads to converge in a victorious relief.
arcs.consequence: Coalition war recovers Hungary and Karlowitz fixes a new frontier farther south-east.
arcs.handoff: Defensive ships, finance and maps now become the equipment of oceanic expansion.

arcs.title: The Atlantic Opens
arcs.situation: Western European kingdoms face the Atlantic as an exposed edge and eastern trade through routes they do not command.
arcs.mechanism: Conquest, island settlement, return winds, repeated reconnaissance and state-held charts turn ocean uncertainty into learned geography.
arcs.turn: The Cape route reaches Calicut by joining Portuguese experience to Indian Ocean pilotage.
arcs.consequence: Europe gains direct strategic access to the Indian Ocean.
arcs.handoff: A second road opens west while royal law tries to divide an ocean still incompletely measured.

arcs.title: The World Road
arcs.situation: Iberian crowns enter lands and oceans their charts and legal lines cannot yet contain.
arcs.mechanism: Atlantic winds, treaty, circumnavigation, cannon, fortified bases, pilot archives and chartered capital make voyages repeatable.
arcs.turn: One surviving ship closes the world's ocean circle and rival European states inherit the routes.
arcs.consequence: The coast becomes a point of departure for a competitive European ocean system.
arcs.handoff: The same print, state capacity and rivalry now divide Latin Christendom at home.

arcs.title: The Argument Escapes
arcs.situation: A university dispute enters a Latin Church whose courts and rulers expect argument to remain governable.
arcs.mechanism: Print, translation, sermon, song, civic ordinance, school and visitation make rival confessions reproducible.
arcs.turn: Catholic renewal answers Protestant institution-building with its own disciplined European programme.
arcs.consequence: Augsburg contains Catholic and Lutheran division while leaving dangerous constitutional fault lines.
arcs.handoff: Bohemian revolt turns those fault lines into a war the confessions cannot control.

arcs.title: The Empire Burns and Survives
arcs.situation: Revolt in Prague joins confession, princely right and dynastic rivalry inside the Empire.
arcs.mechanism: Contribution armies, allied finance, field adaptation, atrocity print and continuous negotiation sustain and eventually contain the war.
arcs.turn: The struggle outlives confession and becomes a European contest over Habsburg power.
arcs.consequence: Westphalia ends the imperial war and preserves religious plurality inside law.
arcs.handoff: The surviving Habsburg crowns build another plural order along the Danube.

arcs.title: The Danube House
arcs.situation: Dynastic succession joins three crowns under Ottoman pressure without merging their laws or political identities.
arcs.mechanism: Frontier service, ratified succession, fiscal knowledge, roads, post, schools and civil office give the monarchy common work.
arcs.turn: Maria Theresa and Joseph make continuous service rather than emergency the vocation of government.
arcs.consequence: Distinct lands acquire a practical common future under one dynasty.
arcs.handoff: The monarchy now enters the age of balance, revolution, constitution and mass transport.

arcs.title: The Braided Monarchy
arcs.situation: Napoleonic war and national politics test whether several crownlands can remain one modern political home.
arcs.mechanism: Diplomacy, emancipation, compromise, rights, court, railway and multilingual municipal life braid the lands together.
arcs.turn: Mass suffrage enlarges participation just before total war replaces bargaining with command and hunger.
arcs.consequence: The common home collapses in 1918, leaving its institutions and routes in successor states.
arcs.handoff: Its measured infrastructure points to the scientific network that taught Europe to accumulate knowledge.

arcs.title: Nature Answers Measure
arcs.situation: Ancient texts command learning while observations of planet and body expose answers the inherited page cannot secure.
arcs.mechanism: Print, dissection, observatory, exact table, glass and quantified demonstration place claims against the world.
arcs.turn: Kepler trusts a measured discrepancy over the perfect circle.
arcs.consequence: Cosmos and body become systems that can be corrected by shared observation.
arcs.handoff: Mathematics and controlled experiment must now make invisible forces portable.

arcs.title: Knowledge Becomes Cumulative
arcs.situation: New observations remain fragile if confined to one instrument, room or investigator.
arcs.mechanism: Geometry, barometer, pump, register, journal, lens and correspondence turn trials into public equipment.
arcs.turn: Societies and printers give a result an address where others can preserve and attack it.
arcs.consequence: Newton can bind earth and sky using a European inheritance accumulated across instruments and minds.
arcs.handoff: The Dutch Republic gathers the shipping, credit, print and information that carry this knowledge.

arcs.title: A Republic Rises
arcs.situation: Revolt controls towns and waterways but lacks one crown capable of commanding all provinces.
arcs.mechanism: Union, migration, efficient shipping, permanent joint capital and common engineering turn distributed authority into capacity.
arcs.turn: Capital remains with the VOC while investors can leave through transferable claims.
arcs.consequence: A small republic gains durable reach over ships, trade and reclaimed land.
arcs.handoff: Its water, money and information now require institutions of trust.

arcs.title: The System of Trust
arcs.situation: Worn coin, distant news, public debt and existential invasion threaten a federation without a royal treasury.
arcs.mechanism: Municipal ledger money, exchange pricing, audited taxation, print and coordinated water defence make cooperation enforceable.
arcs.turn: The republic reverses its own drainage system to stop invasion in 1672.
arcs.consequence: Dutch methods of credit, banking and securities cross the North Sea into a larger constitutional power.
arcs.handoff: The exchange keeps speaking as European information becomes public judgment.

arcs.title: Europe Learns to Compare
arcs.situation: Readers in Europe's cities receive more news, books and foreign examples than any court can wholly command.
arcs.mechanism: Coffeehouse, refugee press, dictionary, periodical, travel and comparative law turn custom and rule into objects of judgment.
arcs.turn: A living foreign arrangement becomes evidence that inherited institutions can be measured against alternatives.
arcs.consequence: Europe acquires a public language for examining how power preserves or destroys liberty.
arcs.handoff: The public now organises knowledge and follows arguments into workshops and statutes.

arcs.title: Opinion Enters Government
arcs.situation: Public judgment possesses reach but must still convert circulation into institutional action.
arcs.mechanism: Encyclopaedia, club, university, penal argument, reform decree and assembly carry thought through collective bodies.
arcs.turn: Beccaria's short book becomes a European legal consequence while palace-controlled reform shows its limit.
arcs.consequence: By 1789 public opinion claims authority to constitute government itself.
arcs.handoff: Material production is meanwhile acquiring its own cumulative engine in British mines and workshops.

arcs.title: Power Multiplies
arcs.situation: Ironmaking, mining and manufacture remain constrained by forest, water site and human scale.
arcs.mechanism: Coke, steam, measured improvement, separate condensation and factory organisation reinforce one another.
arcs.turn: Rotary steam releases the mill from the river's address.
arcs.consequence: Manchester becomes a cluster in which machinery, labour, coal, credit and demand enlarge each other.
arcs.handoff: The system needs stronger iron, faster transport and capital able to outlive a partnership.

arcs.title: Capital Finds a Body
arcs.situation: Industrial works require uniform materials, scheduled movement and fortunes larger than one household can risk.
arcs.mechanism: Rolled iron, railway, exhibition, registration, corporate continuity and limited liability create durable scale.
arcs.turn: Law draws a boundary around subscribed risk without dissolving the company's obligation.
arcs.consequence: Europe can finance projects larger than a private fortune and longer than a working life.
arcs.handoff: Rail becomes cable and carries Europe's industrial and legal system across the world.

arcs.title: The World on Schedule
arcs.situation: Ocean distance still governs trade, information and the enforcement of public purpose.
arcs.mechanism: Fleet, steam packet, submarine cable, canal, telegraph convention, postal union and common time reduce distance through institutions.
arcs.turn: Permanent protocols become as important as wire, ship and engine.
arcs.consequence: Routes and offices across states can recognise the same message, address and hour.
arcs.handoff: The scheduled world now enters continents through survey, railway and administrative city.

arcs.title: Europe at the Central Desk
arcs.situation: European powers seek to measure, connect and govern territories at planetary scale.
arcs.mechanism: Survey, rail, port, school, public health, diplomatic procedure and exhibition join geography to archives and standards.
arcs.turn: London's switchboard receives global action inside one working day.
arcs.consequence: The world possesses a connected institutional order with a European centre.
arcs.handoff: The same switchboard now carries mobilisation into Europe's civil war.

arcs.title: The Armed Peace Breaks
arcs.situation: National unification, mass politics, alliances and conscription create a powerful but brittle continental order.
arcs.mechanism: Rail schedules, administrative mobilisation, industry and household supply compress choice and sustain unprecedented war.
arcs.turn: The expected short campaign becomes a factory of attrition that destroys four empires.
arcs.consequence: Europe's global reach carries its civil war across the world and leaves a shattered imperial map.
arcs.handoff: The peace must turn ruins, national claims and displaced people into a stable legal order.

arcs.title: Total Dominion and Ruin
arcs.situation: Post-war states promise national self-government while millions lose secure membership and plural politics loses authority.
arcs.mechanism: Mass movement, party organisation, racial law, terror, pact, occupation and administrative murder convert state machinery into domination.
arcs.turn: Nazi Germany marks European Jewry for total murder and drives its system toward continental annihilation.
arcs.consequence: Berlin falls, Nazi power is destroyed and Europe loses its old primacy into American and Soviet occupation.
arcs.handoff: Two rival orders rise from the same ruin.

arcs.title: Two Orders Rise
arcs.situation: Europe must restore ordinary government while occupation lines harden into opposed security systems.
arcs.mechanism: American aid, European allocation, Atlantic protection, coal-and-steel authority, market and court bind western recovery.
arcs.turn: Treaty promises enter national courts and survive the governments that signed them.
arcs.consequence: Western Europe creates a cumulative legal and economic order open to restored southern democracies.
arcs.handoff: East of the line, nations must preserve public authority beneath Soviet force.

arcs.title: The East Reclaims the Future
arcs.situation: Soviet power keeps eastern Europe through party, armour, border and enforced public falsehood.
arcs.mechanism: Revolt, reform, church, pilgrimage, independent print, elected representation and negotiation preserve national and moral community.
arcs.turn: Solidarity survives martial law and forces the Polish party back to the table.
arcs.consequence: Eastern Europeans open borders, elections and streets until the divided roads meet in 1989.
arcs.handoff: Recovered nations choose European law and Atlantic defence while Russia contests their choice.

arcs.title: The Return Is Chosen
arcs.situation: Freed eastern nations recover statehood and seek durable entry into the institutions of the West.
arcs.mechanism: Constitutional reform, accession criteria, treaty ratification and alliance planning move Union law and Article Five east by consent.
arcs.turn: Russia invades Georgia and Ukraine's citizens defend their European constitutional choice on the Maidan.
arcs.consequence: The post-1989 settlement is revealed as a sovereign choice that external force intends to reverse.
arcs.handoff: Russia seizes Crimea and opens the war that will become a full-scale invasion.

arcs.title: The Line Is Held
arcs.situation: Russia occupies Ukrainian territory and uses an unfinished war to constrain Ukraine's future.
arcs.mechanism: Ukrainian defence, Union candidacy, allied support, NATO enlargement, accession work and continental logistics convert choice into endurance.
arcs.turn: Kyiv refuses to fall and preserves the Ukrainian state.
arcs.consequence: Europe rebuilds the legal, industrial and military capacity to sustain an open order at its eastern line.
arcs.handoff: The route returns to the living world with the line illuminated because institutions and nations continue to hold it.
